spoken: runbook for database failover, if the primary postgresql instance becomes unavailable the replica is promoted automatically within about thirty seconds, um you should still verify by running the status command and checking that the new primary reports in recovery false, after failover update the connection string in the kubernetes secret, er the old primary should not be restarted until the data has been compared, datadog will page the on call engineer if replication lag exceeds sixty seconds, and the escalation contact after that is the database team lead, the full process should take under fifteen minutes
intended: Runbook for database failover: if the primary PostgreSQL instance becomes unavailable, the replica is promoted automatically within about 30 seconds. You should still verify by running the status command and checking that the new primary reports "in recovery: false." After failover, update the connection string in the Kubernetes secret. The old primary should not be restarted until the data has been compared. Datadog will page the on-call engineer if replication lag exceeds 60 seconds, and the escalation contact after that is the database team lead. The full process should take under 15 minutes.

spoken: design doc caching layer for the catalog service, background, er the catalog api currently serves about nine thousand requests per second at peak and every request hits postgresql, which means the database cpu is at seventy percent during sales, um the goal is to bring that under thirty percent without changing the api, proposal, um we add a redis cache in front of the read path with a time to live of two minutes, no wait five minutes for product details and thirty seconds for inventory, uh since inventory changes faster, the redis cluster will have three nodes and will be provisioned with terraform and deployed alongside the services on kubernetes, er cache invalidation happens on write through a message on the event bus, risks, a cold cache after a deploy could send a spike of traffic to the database, so we will warm the cache for the top ten thousand products before shifting traffic, rollout, we start at five percent of traffic, then twenty five, then a hundred over about two weeks
intended:
Design doc: Caching layer for the catalog service

Background: The catalog API currently serves about 9,000 requests per second at peak, and every request hits PostgreSQL, which means the database CPU is at 70% during sales. The goal is to bring that under 30% without changing the API.

Proposal: We add a Redis cache in front of the read path with a time-to-live of 5 minutes for product details and 30 seconds for inventory, since inventory changes faster. The Redis cluster will have three nodes and will be provisioned with Terraform and deployed alongside the services on Kubernetes. Cache invalidation happens on write through a message on the event bus.

Risks: A cold cache after a deploy could send a spike of traffic to the database, so we will warm the cache for the top 10,000 products before shifting traffic.

Rollout: We start at 5% of traffic, then 25%, then 100% over about two weeks.
